D: A boy who dreams of music ends up in the Land of the Dead on the Day of the Dead.
P: Serve the tamales when Abuelita insists Miguel eat more.
S: she keeps piling them on his plate
Masa beaten with lard, stock and baking powder until fluffy, spread on soaked corn husks, filled with chicken in a red chilli sauce, folded and steamed 75 minutes.
the bridge of orange petals to the Land of the Dead
Corn cobs grilled until charred, rolled in mayo and lime, covered in crumbled feta, chilli powder and coriander, a few marigold-coloured nasturtium petals on top.
Santa Cecilia plaza guacamole and totopos
the mariachi plaza in Santa Cecilia

Chunky guacamole with lime, chilli, onion and coriander, topped with pomegranate and toasted pepitas, with crisp fried corn tortilla chips. Cut 8 corn tortillas into wedges and fry at 180C for 2 minutes until crisp, then salt. Mash 3 ripe avocados roughly with the juice of 2 limes and salt. Fold in half a finely diced white onion, 1 seeded chopped jalapeño, 1 diced tomato and a handful of coriander. Top with 2 tbsp pomegranate seeds and 2 tbsp toasted pepitas and serve with the warm chips.
M: the family's Day of the Dead table

Pork shoulder and hominy simmered in a deep red chilli broth, topped at the table with shredded cabbage, radish, lime, oregano and crisp tostadas. Simmer 1.2kg diced pork shoulder in 2.5 litres water with 1 halved onion, 4 garlic cloves and 2 tsp salt for 1.5 hours. Soak 4 dried guajillo and 2 ancho chillies in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend with 2 garlic cloves and a little soaking water and strain into the pot. Add 2 drained tins hominy and simmer 30 minutes more. Serve with shredded cabbage, sliced radish, lime wedges, dried oregano and tostadas.
Corn tortillas dipped in red chilli sauce, rolled around shredded chicken and cheese, covered in more sauce and cheese, baked at 190C for 20 minutes. Crema and onion.
W: Enriched yeasted dough with orange zest and orange blossom, shaped into rounds with dough "bones" on top, baked at 180C for 30 minutes, brushed with butter and rolled in sugar.
K: the thick chocolate drink of the season
Masa harina whisked into hot milk with Mexican-style chocolate, cinnamon and brown sugar, simmered until thick and silky.

s.note: the bridge of orange petals to the Land of the Dead
s.how: Grill 4 corn cobs until charred. Brush with 4 tbsp mayo mixed with lime juice. Roll in 100g crumbled feta, dust with chilli powder and coriander, and scatter a few orange nasturtium petals on top.

s.note: she keeps piling them on his plate
s.how: Simmer 500g pork shoulder until tender, shred and mix with 4 tbsp red chilli sauce. Beat 300g masa harina with 100g lard, 1 tsp baking powder and 400ml warm stock to a soft dough. Spread on 16 soaked corn husks, add pork, fold and steam 60 minutes. Serve with salsa.

m.how: Soak 4 dried chillies, blitz with a garlic clove and 300ml stock and simmer. Poach and shred 600g chicken thighs. Dip 8 corn tortillas in sauce, roll with chicken and 100g cheese, cover with sauce and 100g more cheese. Bake at 190C for 20 minutes.

w.how: Mix 450g flour, 7g yeast, 80g sugar, orange zest, 3 eggs, 80g soft butter and 100ml warm water and prove 2 hours. Shape 6 rounds with dough bones on top, prove again and bake at 180C for 30 minutes. Brush with 40g butter and roll in sugar.

d.note: the thick chocolate drink of the season
d.how: Whisk 50g masa harina into 250ml water until smooth. Heat 1L milk with 100g dark chocolate, a cinnamon stick and 60g brown sugar, then whisk in the masa. Simmer, stirring, until thick and silky. Pour into mugs.
